question: A man sold an article for ₹217, there by gaining 8.5%. The cost of the article (in ₹) was:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Fraction equivalent of 8.5% = 8.5 ÷ 100 = 17 ÷ 200

Let Cost Price (CP) = 200 units, then Gain = 17 units.

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Gain = 200 + 17 = 217 units.

Given 217 units = ₹217 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹1

Cost Price = 200 units = 200 × 1 = ₹200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Selling Price (SP) of the article = ₹217

⇒ Gain percentage = 8.5%

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = [100 ÷ (100 + Gain%)] × SP

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 CP = ?
 (100%)
 
 
 SP = ₹217
 (108.5%)

 

 + 8.5% Gain
 
 CP = (217 ÷ 108.5) × 100 = ₹200

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = [100 ÷ (100 + 8.5)] × 217

⇒ CP = (100 ÷ 108.5) × 217

⇒ CP = (1000 ÷ 1085) × 217

⇒ CP = (200 ÷ 217) × 217

⇒ CP = 200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage Formula

When an article is sold below its cost price, the loss percentage is calculated as: Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of the item. The effective Selling Price is determined by: SP = MP × [1 − (Discount% ÷ 100)].

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of x% and y% are applied, the equivalent single discount percentage is given by: [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%.
